rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Big Idea leads with the positive discipline (durable encoding of a found gap), not a failure word. Failure (finding the same gap again next week) is the negative case the discipline addresses, correctly subordinated to the lead clause.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strategy-fidelity — consolidates front-run check, module-to-module arc, Big Idea fidelity, mood-doesn't-resolve-early.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Front-run: opener order is 'The 2 frontiers' then 'Story of Module 6' — this is maintainer-confirmed correct (2026-08-12) and the strategy doc has been corrected to match; not re-flagged per explicit dispatch instruction. Big Idea fidelity: Key Concepts and What You'll Learn both cash out the Big Idea's 'somewhere durable' claim into the three-homes taxonomy, no drift. Module-to-module arc: 'Next' section hands forward to the student's own future send-offs rather than fabricating a false M7 handoff (M7 is optional per strategy doc), which is the correct shape for a core-arc close. Mood-doesn't-resolve-early: this is the training's LAST core module, so 'resolving early' doesn't apply the way it would mid-arc — the close is meant to land the arc, not defer it.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No cross-module sequencing in lecture bodies.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide/lecture headers pass the squint test and the truth clause.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule targets concept-naming slide headers inside lecture files. This module file's own `##` headers (Big Idea, Prework, What You'll Learn, Start here, Key Concepts, Human close, Next) are structural/navigational section labels, not concept-argument headers of the kind the squint test is built to catch — no header here claims a concept the body might not support.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slide's body is size-bounded — under ~210 readable words AND ≤6 bullets per `##`.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Mechanical check (`node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md`) reports `## What You'll Learn` at 91 words (well under the word cap) but 7 bullets (Diagnose/Read/Cut/Surface/Map/Encode/Generalize) against the 6-bullet cap — the script's default gate exits 1 on this file. Harm check: the harm this rule guards is per-`##`-slide projection legibility in the classroom deck; a 7th bullet is exactly the kind of overflow the cap exists to catch, and unlike the file's Key Concepts section (which the maintainer block explicitly attests sits 'at the bullet cap' at 6), this section carries no accept-note — it reads as an unnoticed drift, not a deliberate exception. All three persona reads independently noticed the list running longer than the arc's other capability lists (mid-layer: 'takes a beat longer to skim'; senior: 'first list that reads like a checklist'), which is consistent with the mechanical finding rather than contradicting it.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Merge two of the seven verbs whose outputs are closely paired (Surface + Map are both stack-scan outputs feeding the same close-lecture handoff) into one bullet, or fold one clause into an adjacent bullet's tail — author's call in /content-creation, not a rewrite from this judge.
